claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start the assessment, I need to know about your child(ren):

**How old is the child (or children) that you're asking about?**

The eligibility rules differ based on age:
- **Under 16 years old** – automatic qualification (subject to other conditions)
- **16-19 years old** – must be in full-time education or training
- **20 years old or over** – not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me the age(s) of the child or children you're inquiring about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son **Alex, who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age group, I need to check whether he meets the education or training requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

This could include:
- Full-time education at school, college, or university
- An approved apprenticeship or training scheme
- Other qualifying training

Please let me know his current status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and hasn't gone on to college or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has left education but isn't in any training programme at the moment.

Since Alex has recently left education, there may still be a possibility of eligibility through an extension period. Let me check this:

**How long ago did Alex finish school?**

Child Benefit can sometimes be extended for a limited period after leaving full-time education. I need to know if he left within a qualifying timeframe to determine if an extension applies.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see from the rules that there's an extension period of **20 weeks** after leaving full-time education. This means if Alex left school within the last 20 weeks, he may still qualify.

**When exactly did Alex finish school?** (Please provide the approximate date or how many weeks/months ago)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school back in June last year, so that would be about 8 or 9 months ago now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Unfortunately, that's outside the qualifying extension period.

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a young person leaves full-time education, there is an extension period of **20 weeks** during which they can still qualify. Since Alex left school in June (approximately 8-9 months ago), he is well beyond that 20-week extension window.

This means Alex no longer qualifies as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes.

Let me provide you with your final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Decision

**Result: NOT ELIGIBLE**

---

**Summary for Alex:**
- **Age:** 17 years old
- **Status:** Not in full-time education or training
- **Decision:** Not eligible for Child Benefit

---

**Why Alex doesn't qualify:**

Child Benefit for 16-19 year olds requires them to be in full-time education or approved training. While there is a grace period of **20 weeks** after leaving education, Alex left school in June (approximately 8-9 months ago), which is well beyond this extension window.

---

**What happens next?**

If Alex were to return to full-time education or start an approved training course, he could potentially become eligible again. Otherwise, Child Benefit eligibility would not resume for him at this time.

If you have any other questions or if there are other children you'd like to ask about, I'm happy to help!
